Sourced from: GKE Agent Sandbox docs, kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox

So here is the thing. We are asking AI agents to do increasingly wild stuff. Write code. Browse the web. Run shell commands. Spin up browsers. Click around. Deploy websites. Use a computer like a human would. And for the most part, they are doing it.

But there is a lurking problem that keeps platform engineers up at night.

Where the hell is this code running?

When you ask an agent to "run this script" or "install this package" or "check if that endpoint responds", you are effectively handing over a loaded gun to a very enthusiastic intern who has read every programming book but has absolutely zero survival instincts. That code could be malicious. Or buggy. Or it could just go nuclear on your host system because the agent decided to rm -rf / thinking it was cleaning up temp files.

That is where Agent Sandboxes come in.

Think of them as giving each agent its own airtight, disposable Linux container. A little VM crib. A playpen with rubber walls where they can run around and break things without ever touching your real infrastructure.

And here is the kicker: this is not some vaporware future concept. Google Cloud ships Agent Sandbox as a managed GKE feature, and the open-source project behind the Kubernetes APIs lives under kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox. You can run the open-source controller on your own Kubernetes cluster or use the managed GKE integration.

What GKE Agent Sandbox Actually Is

Let me quote the docs directly so we are on the same page:

"GKE Agent Sandbox helps you manage isolated, stateful, and single-replica workloads on GKE. It is optimized for use cases like AI agent runtimes, where untrusted, LLM-generated code must be executed in a secure and performant environment."

What that means in plain English is:

You get a Kubernetes-native way to spin up a single, stateful container that behaves like a lightweight VM. It has a stable hostname, persistent storage that survives restarts, kernel-level isolation, and network policies that default to "deny all". Your agent can connect to it, do its thing, disconnect, come back later, and find everything exactly as it left it. Or it can get garbage collected after a TTL and disappear without a trace.

With a SandboxWarmPool, already-started sandboxes can be assigned in milliseconds instead of waiting for a cold Pod to schedule, pull an image, and start. Cold-start latency still depends on your cluster, scheduler, image, and runtime.

The Architecture: CRDs All the Way Down

The whole thing is built on Kubernetes custom resource definitions. There are four main ones that matter:

1. Sandbox (the core)

This is the primitive. A single, stateful Pod with a stable hostname, optional persistent storage, and full lifecycle management. You create this, and the controller handles the rest -- Pod creation, network identity, volume provisioning, scheduled deletion, pausing, and resuming.

It is the answer to the question: "I want a Linux box that stays alive for my agent. How do I get one?"

2. SandboxTemplate (the blueprint)

Tired of writing the same YAML over and over? Templates let you codify runtime configuration once -- image, resource limits, runtime class (gVisor, Kata, standard), network policies, environment variables -- and reuse them everywhere. Platform teams define the templates. Developers just pick one and go.

3. SandboxClaim (the request)

This is the user-facing abstraction. In the current v1beta1 API, a developer or agent SDK creates a SandboxClaim that references a SandboxWarmPool. The warm pool references the SandboxTemplate. The controller adopts an available pre-warmed sandbox from that pool, or creates capacity according to the pool configuration, and hands back a ready-to-use environment.

This is the Claim Model in action. You separate the what (I need a sandbox) from the how (here is where it runs on the cluster). And honestly? This is the pattern Kubernetes has needed for stateful workloads for a long time.

4. SandboxWarmPool (the performance hack)

Here is where it gets fast. A SandboxWarmPool maintains a set of pre-warmed Pod instances in a ready state. When a claim comes in, the controller instantly assigns a Pod from the pool instead of waiting for image pulls and container startup.

Warm pools reduce provisioning latency by keeping Sandbox instances pre-created and ready to be claimed. On GKE, Pod snapshots are a separate feature that can save and restore sandbox state for pause/resume and faster recovery; they are not required for a warm pool to work.

Security: Default Deny Is the Only Way

Here is something that does not get talked about enough. When you give an agent a Linux box, you are trusting it with network access. A lot of agent sandbox solutions just throw a container at you and say "good luck".

GKE Agent Sandbox implements a Default Deny network security posture. Out of the box, code inside a sandbox cannot access your internal networks, your GKE control plane, or anything it should not. You explicitly define allowed egress and ingress rules in your SandboxTemplate.

Why does this matter? Because the most realistic threat from LLM-generated code is not "the AI becomes self-aware and takes over the world". It is "the AI wrote a Python script with a typo that accidentally hit the production database". Default deny prevents the accident. Fine-grained rules let you open specific doors when you need to (e.g., pip needs to reach PyPI, your agent needs to call an API).

Isolation Runtimes: Pick Your Poison

The Sandbox CRD is runtime-agnostic. You can pair it with:

  • Standard containers -- fast, familiar, but minimal isolation between workloads
  • gVisor -- Google's user-space kernel. Gives you a second security boundary between your container and the host kernel. This is the recommended default for untrusted code execution.
  • Kata Containers -- hardware-level VM isolation. Each sandbox gets its own lightweight VM with its own kernel. The heaviest isolation, but also the strongest.

The beauty of the API is that switching between these is a field change in your SandboxTemplate. You do not redesign your architecture. You just change runtimeClassName.

Programmatic Access SDKs

You do not need to write Kubernetes YAML to use this. There are first-class client libraries:

  • Python SDK -- high-level client for LangChain, Vertex AI Agentic SDK, or any Python agent framework. Create, query, manage, and destroy sandboxes from your agent code.
  • Go SDK -- for platform engineers building controllers and services on top of Agent Sandbox.

Both SDKs abstract away the claim lifecycle. With the current Python SDK, your agent creates a sandbox with client.create_sandbox(warmpool="python-sandbox-pool", namespace="default"). Behind the scenes, the SDK creates a SandboxClaim, the controller assigns a Sandbox from the warm pool, and the client returns a handle for command execution and file operations.

The Comparison Table

Feature GKE Agent Sandbox (managed) kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox (open source)
Type Managed GKE add-on Self-installed Kubernetes controller
CRDs Sandbox, SandboxTemplate, SandboxClaim, SandboxWarmPool Sandbox, SandboxTemplate, SandboxClaim, SandboxWarmPool
Provisioning speed Warm pools reduce claim latency to millisecond-scale assignment Varies by cluster; warm pools avoid cold-start work
Isolation runtimes gVisor is required for managed Agent Sandbox workloads Runtime-agnostic through Kubernetes runtimeClassName
Network security Default deny, fine-grained egress/ingress rules Configurable via standard K8s NetworkPolicies
Snapshots GKE Pod snapshots integrate with pause/resume Platform/runtime dependent; not required for warm pools
SDKs Python + Go Python + Go
Lifecycle mgmt Managed by Google (upgrades, patches) Self-managed via controller
Limitations Requires GKE 1.35.2-gke.1269000+ for full feature support Compatibility is release-specific; pin and test a release
Licensing Google Cloud SLA Apache 2.0
Best for Google Cloud native teams who want "it just works" Multi-cloud, self-managed, air-gapped environments

The Practical Takeaway

Agent Sandbox solves a real problem that has been getting more urgent by the month. As LLMs get better at generating code, the volume of untrusted code being executed in agent loops is going to explode. Every one of those executions is an opportunity for something to go wrong.

The old approach was: "just run it in a Docker container, it will be fine." A container can absolutely have a hostname and persistent volumes, but a one-off Docker workflow does not give you the Kubernetes-native Sandbox lifecycle, claim/warm-pool allocation model, controller-managed identity, or stronger isolation runtime by itself. Those are the abstractions Agent Sandbox is adding.

Agent Sandbox gives you those lifecycle and allocation primitives on top of Kubernetes, with SDKs in Python and Go. Isolation strength still depends on the runtime you configure; the managed GKE feature enforces gVisor for sandbox workloads.

The open-source project under kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox is the bedrock. Google's managed GKE add-on is the "press this button and it works" version. Both are worth knowing about.

A Reality Check (Because Nothing Is Perfect)

Latency is low but not zero. Even with warm pools and Pod snapshots, you are looking at hundreds of milliseconds to a second for sandbox assignment. For most agent use cases that is fine. For real-time loops that need sub-100ms responses, you will feel it.

State management is your problem. A sandbox is stateful by design. But what happens when an agent session crashes mid-execution? Do you keep the sandbox around? For how long? The TTL feature helps, but designing your garbage collection strategy is on you.

Network policy complexity is real. Default deny is great for security. But the first time your agent cannot pip install because egress to PyPI is blocked, you will spend time debugging. And the first time a client's script needs to reach an internal API, you will be writing policy rules. It is manageable. But it is not zero-effort.

Costs add up in warm pools. Each pre-warmed Pod is a running container burning CPU and memory while it waits. If you keep a pool of 20 sandboxes hot, you are paying for 20 idle containers. The pause/resume via Pod snapshots helps offset this, but it is something to budget for.

Monitoring is a blank canvas. Your existing Kubernetes monitoring? Probably set up for Deployments and StatefulSets. Ephemeral sandboxes that live for seconds to minutes are a different monitoring challenge. Log aggregation, metrics collection, cost attribution -- you are building some of this yourself.

Getting Started

If you want to reproduce the open-source setup on a fresh Kubernetes cluster, the sequence below is complete: install the controller and extensions, create an executable Python runtime template, create a warm pool, give an in-cluster client the required RBAC, and run the SDK from a normal Python Pod.

The commands below intentionally use kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF' so you do not need to write YAML files locally.

1. Install Agent Sandbox with the extension CRDs

As of this writing, the current upstream release is v0.5.3. Pinning the version makes the example reproducible instead of silently changing when a new release lands.

export VERSION="v0.5.3"

kubectl apply -f \
  https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/releases/download/${VERSION}/sandbox-with-extensions.yaml

Wait for the controller components to come up:

kubectl get pods -n agent-sandbox-system

Verify that both the core and extension APIs are installed:

kubectl api-resources | grep -i sandbox

You should see resources including sandboxes, sandboxclaims, sandboxtemplates, and sandboxwarmpools.

2. Create a Python runtime template and warm pool

A plain python:3.12-slim container with sleep infinity is not enough for sandbox.commands.run(). The SDK sends HTTP requests to the runtime's /execute endpoint on port 8888, so the sandbox image must implement that API.

The upstream Python runtime image does exactly that:

kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: SandboxTemplate
metadata:
  name: python-sandbox-template
  namespace: default
spec:
  podTemplate:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: python-sandbox
        image: registry.k8s.io/agent-sandbox/python-runtime-sandbox:v0.1.0
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8888
---
apiVersion: extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: SandboxWarmPool
metadata:
  name: python-sandbox-pool
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  sandboxTemplateRef:
    name: python-sandbox-template
EOF

Verify that the template, pool, Sandbox, and Pod exist:

kubectl get sandboxtemplates,sandboxwarmpools,sandboxes,pods -n default

Wait until the warm-pool sandbox Pod is Running.

3. Create a dedicated ServiceAccount and RBAC for the SDK client

Do not run the SDK with the namespace's default ServiceAccount in a real deployment. Give the client its own ServiceAccount with the permissions it needs to create/delete claims and resolve the underlying Sandbox.

kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: sandbox-client
  namespace: default
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: sandbox-client
  namespace: default
rules:
- apiGroups:
  - agents.x-k8s.io
  resources:
  - sandboxes
  verbs:
  - get
  - list
  - watch
- apiGroups:
  - extensions.agents.x-k8s.io
  resources:
  - sandboxclaims
  verbs:
  - get
  - list
  - watch
  - create
  - delete
- apiGroups:
  - extensions.agents.x-k8s.io
  resources:
  - sandboxwarmpools
  - sandboxtemplates
  verbs:
  - get
  - list
  - watch
- apiGroups:
  - ""
  resources:
  - pods
  - services
  verbs:
  - get
  - list
  - watch
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: sandbox-client
  namespace: default
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: sandbox-client
  namespace: default
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: sandbox-client
EOF

Verify the critical permissions using the fully qualified resource name syntax supported by kubectl auth can-i:

kubectl auth can-i get sandboxes.agents.x-k8s.io \
  --as=system:serviceaccount:default:sandbox-client \
  -n default

kubectl auth can-i create sandboxclaims.extensions.agents.x-k8s.io \
  --as=system:serviceaccount:default:sandbox-client \
  -n default

kubectl auth can-i delete sandboxclaims.extensions.agents.x-k8s.io \
  --as=system:serviceaccount:default:sandbox-client \
  -n default

All three should return yes.

4. Start a Python client Pod

The SDK can run locally using kubectl port-forward, but that mode requires kubectl in the environment running the Python process. For this reproducible example, run the client inside the cluster and use SandboxInClusterConnectionConfig, which connects directly to the sandbox runtime and does not spawn kubectl.

kubectl run python-pod \
  --image=python:3.12-slim \
  --restart=Never \
  --overrides='{"spec":{"serviceAccountName":"sandbox-client"}}' \
  --command -- sleep infinity

Wait for it:

kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/python-pod -n default --timeout=120s

Install the Python SDK in that Pod, pinned to the controller release used above:

kubectl exec -n default python-pod -- \
  pip install k8s-agent-sandbox==0.5.3

5. Create a sandbox and execute Python inside it

Run the client directly through stdin; no Python file is required:

kubectl exec -i -n default python-pod -- python - <<'PY'
from k8s_agent_sandbox import SandboxClient
from k8s_agent_sandbox.models import SandboxInClusterConnectionConfig

client = SandboxClient(
    connection_config=SandboxInClusterConnectionConfig()
)

sandbox = client.create_sandbox(
    warmpool="python-sandbox-pool",
    namespace="default",
)

try:
    result = sandbox.commands.run(
        'python3 -c \'print("hello from my sandbox")\''
    )
    print(result.stdout)
finally:
    sandbox.terminate()
PY

Expected output:

hello from my sandbox

At this point the complete path is working:

python-pod
    |
    | SandboxInClusterConnectionConfig
    v
SandboxClaim -> SandboxWarmPool -> Sandbox -> runtime Pod:8888
                                      |
                                      +-> POST /execute

6. Troubleshooting the three failures you are most likely to hit

If you get:

SandboxWarmPoolNotFoundError: SandboxWarmPool "python-sandbox-pool" not found

check that the warm pool exists in the same namespace:

kubectl get sandboxwarmpools -n default

If you get a 403 Forbidden mentioning sandboxclaims or sandboxes, check the ServiceAccount RBAC:

kubectl auth can-i get sandboxes.agents.x-k8s.io \
  --as=system:serviceaccount:default:sandbox-client \
  -n default

If you get:

HTTPConnection(... port=8888): Failed to establish a new connection: Connection refused

check the image used by the sandbox Pod:

kubectl get pods -n default \
  -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,IMAGE:.spec.containers[*].image,IP:.status.podIP

The sandbox must run a runtime server that implements /execute on port 8888; a normal Python image that only sleeps will not work with sandbox.commands.run().

7. Clean up 

kubectl delete pod python-pod -n default --ignore-not-found
kubectl delete sandboxwarmpool python-sandbox-pool -n default --ignore-not-found
kubectl delete sandboxtemplate python-sandbox-template -n default --ignore-not-found
kubectl delete rolebinding sandbox-client -n default --ignore-not-found
kubectl delete role sandbox-client -n default --ignore-not-found
kubectl delete serviceaccount sandbox-client -n default --ignore-not-found

On GKE instead

For the managed GKE feature, Agent Sandbox requires GKE 1.35.2-gke.1269000 or later. On an existing Standard cluster, Google also requires a gVisor-enabled node pool before enabling Agent Sandbox. The current command uses the beta cluster surface and includes the cluster location:

gcloud beta container clusters update "${CLUSTER_NAME}" \
  --location="${LOCATION}" \
  --enable-agent-sandbox

GKE additionally enforces sandbox workload requirements such as runtimeClassName: gvisor, disabling automatic ServiceAccount-token mounting, running as non-root, dropping Linux capabilities, setting CPU/memory limits, and scheduling onto the gVisor sandbox node pool. Use the managed GKE deployment manifest from the official GKE guide rather than the minimal self-managed template above.

The Bottom Line

GKE Agent Sandbox -- and the open-source kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox project it is built on -- is what happens when someone finally builds the right abstraction for agent runtimes. It is Kubernetes-native, which means it fits into existing infrastructure without fighting it. It is fast enough for interactive use. It is secure by default. And it has SDKs that let agents manage their own environments programmatically.

The era of "just run it in Docker and pray" is ending. The era of "give the agent its own Linux box, properly isolated, properly managed, properly fast" is here.

And honestly? It is about damn time.

All the sourcing for this post:

  • GKE Agent Sandbox documentation -- the primary source on the managed GKE add-on
  • kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox (~3k stars) -- the open-source CNCF SIG project under SIG Apps
  • Agent Sandbox documentation site -- full docs, getting started guides, Python/Go SDK references
  • Agent Sandbox Python SDK -- programmatic sandbox management from Python
  • Agent Sandbox Go SDK -- same, but for Go

The upstream Python runtime image does exactly that: kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF' apiVersion: extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1 kind: SandboxTemplate metadata: name: python-sandbox-template namespace: default spec: podTemplate: spec: containers: - name: python-sandbox image: registry.k8s.io/agent-sandbox/python-runtime-sandbox:v0.1.0 imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent ports: - containerPort: 8888 --- apiVersion: extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1 kind: SandboxWarmPool metadata: name: python-sandbox-pool namespace: default spec: replicas: 1 sandboxTemplateRef: name: python-sandbox-template EOF Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Verify that the template, pool, Sandbox, and Pod exist: kubectl get sandboxtemplates,sandboxwarmpools,sandboxes,pods -n default Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Wait until the warm-pool sandbox Pod is Running. 3. Create a dedicated ServiceAccount and RBAC for the SDK client Do not run the SDK with the namespace's default ServiceAccount in a real deployment. Give the client its own ServiceAccount with the permissions it needs to create/delete claims and resolve the underlying Sandbox. kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF' apiVersion: v1 kind: ServiceAccount metadata: name: sandbox-client namespace: default --- apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: Role metadata: name: sandbox-client namespace: default rules: - apiGroups: - agents.x-k8s.io resources: - sandboxes verbs: - get - list - watch - apiGroups: - extensions.agents.x-k8s.io resources: - sandboxclaims verbs: - get - list - watch - create - delete - apiGroups: - extensions.agents.x-k8s.io resources: - sandboxwarmpools - sandboxtemplates verbs: - get - list - watch - apiGroups: - "" resources: - pods - services verbs: - get - list - watch --- apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: RoleBinding metadata: name: sandbox-client namespace: default subjects: - kind: ServiceAccount name: sandbox-client namespace: default roleRef: apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io kind: Role name: sandbox-client EOF Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Verify the critical permissions using the fully qualified resource name syntax supported by kubectl auth can-i: kubectl auth can-i get sandboxes.agents.x-k8s.io \ --as=system:serviceaccount:default:sandbox-client \ -n default kubectl auth can-i create sandboxclaims.extensions.agents.x-k8s.io \ --as=system:serviceaccount:default:sandbox-client \ -n default kubectl auth can-i delete sandboxclaims.extensions.agents.x-k8s.io \ --as=system:serviceaccount:default:sandbox-client \ -n default Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode All three should return yes. 4. Start a Python client Pod The SDK can run locally using kubectl port-forward, but that mode requires kubectl in the environment running the Python process. For this reproducible example, run the client inside the cluster and use SandboxInClusterConnectionConfig, which connects directly to the sandbox runtime and does not spawn kubectl. kubectl run python-pod \ --image=python:3.12-slim \ --restart=Never \ --overrides='{"spec":{"serviceAccountName":"sandbox-client"}}' \ --command -- sleep infinity Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Wait for it: kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/python-pod -n default --timeout=120s Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Install the Python SDK in that Pod, pinned to the controller release used above: kubectl exec -n default python-pod -- \ pip install k8s-agent-sandbox==0.5.3 Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode 5. Create a sandbox and execute Python inside it Run the client directly through stdin; no Python file is required: kubectl exec -i -n default python-pod -- python - <<'PY' from k8s_agent_sandbox import SandboxClient from k8s_agent_sandbox.models import SandboxInClusterConnectionConfig client = SandboxClient( connection_config=SandboxInClusterConnectionConfig() ) sandbox = client.create_sandbox( warmpool="python-sandbox-pool", namespace="default", ) try: result = sandbox.commands.run( 'python3 -c \'print("hello from my sandbox")\'' ) print(result.stdout) finally: sandbox.terminate() PY Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Expected output: hello from my sandbox Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode At this point the complete path is working: python-pod | | SandboxInClusterConnectionConfig v SandboxClaim -> SandboxWarmPool -> Sandbox -> runtime Pod:8888 | +-> POST /execute Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode 6. Troubleshooting the three failures you are most likely to hit If you get: SandboxWarmPoolNotFoundError: SandboxWarmPool "python-sandbox-pool" not found Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode check that the warm pool exists in the same namespace: kubectl get sandboxwarmpools -n default Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode If you get a 403 Forbidden mentioning sandboxclaims or sandboxes, check the ServiceAccount RBAC: kubectl auth can-i get sandboxes.agents.x-k8s.io \ --as=system:serviceaccount:default:sandbox-client \ -n default Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode If you get: HTTPConnection(... port=8888): Failed to establish a new connection: Connection refused Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode check the image used by the sandbox Pod: kubectl get pods -n default \ -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,IMAGE:.spec.containers[*].image,IP:.status.podIP Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode The sandbox must run a runtime server that implements /execute on port 8888; a normal Python image that only sleeps will not work with sandbox.commands.run(). 7. Clean up kubectl delete pod python-pod -n default --ignore-not-found kubectl delete sandboxwarmpool python-sandbox-pool -n default --ignore-not-found kubectl delete sandboxtemplate python-sandbox-template -n default --ignore-not-found kubectl delete rolebinding sandbox-client -n default --ignore-not-found kubectl delete role sandbox-client -n default --ignore-not-found kubectl delete serviceaccount sandbox-client -n default --ignore-not-found Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode On GKE instead For the managed GKE feature, Agent Sandbox requires GKE 1.35.2-gke.1269000 or later. On an existing Standard cluster, Google also requires a gVisor-enabled node pool before enabling Agent Sandbox. The current command uses the beta cluster surface and includes the cluster location: gcloud beta container clusters update "${CLUSTER_NAME}" \ --location="${LOCATION}" \ --enable-agent-sandbox Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode GKE additionally enforces sandbox workload requirements such as runtimeClassName: gvisor, disabling automatic ServiceAccount-token mounting, running as non-root, dropping Linux capabilities, setting CPU/memory limits, and scheduling onto the gVisor sandbox node pool. Use the managed GKE deployment manifest from the official GKE guide rather than the minimal self-managed template above. The Bottom Line GKE Agent Sandbox -- and the open-source kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox project it is built on -- is what happens when someone finally builds the right abstraction for agent runtimes. It is Kubernetes-native, which means it fits into existing infrastructure without fighting it. It is fast enough for interactive use. It is secure by default. And it has SDKs that let agents manage their own environments programmatically. The era of "just run it in Docker and pray" is ending. The era of "give the agent its own Linux box, properly isolated, properly managed, properly fast" is here. And honestly? It is about damn time. That code could be malicious. Or buggy. Or it could just go nuclear on your host system because the agent decided to rm -rf / thinking it was cleaning up temp files.

blocks.html_en: That is where Agent Sandboxes come in.

blocks.html_en: Think of them as giving each agent its own airtight, disposable Linux container. A little VM crib. A playpen with rubber walls where they can run around and break things without ever touching your real infrastructure.

sentences.en: What GKE Agent Sandbox Actually Is

blocks.html_en: "GKE Agent Sandbox helps you manage isolated, stateful, and single-replica workloads on GKE. It is optimized for use cases like AI agent runtimes, where untrusted, LLM-generated code must be executed in a secure and performant environment."

blocks.html_en: What that means in plain English is:

sentences.en: What that means in plain English is:
sentences.zh: 用简单的英语来说，这意味着：

blocks.html_en: You get a Kubernetes-native way to spin up a single, stateful container that behaves like a lightweight VM. It has a stable hostname, persistent storage that survives restarts, kernel-level isolation, and network policies that default to "deny all". Your agent can connect to it, do its thing, disconnect, come back later, and find everything exactly as it left it. Or it can get garbage collected after a TTL and disappear without a trace.

sentences.en: You get a Kubernetes-native way to spin up a single, stateful container that behaves like a lightweight VM.
sentences.zh: 您可以通过 Kubernetes 原生方式来启动单个有状态容器，其行为类似于轻量级虚拟机。

sentences.en: It has a stable hostname, persistent storage that survives restarts, kernel-level isolation, and network policies that default to "deny all".
sentences.zh: 它具有稳定的主机名、可在重新启动后继续存在的持久存储、内核级隔离以及默认为“拒绝所有”的网络策略。

sentences.en: Your agent can connect to it, do its thing, disconnect, come back later, and find everything exactly as it left it.
sentences.zh: 您的代理可以连接到它，执行其操作，断开连接，稍后再回来，并找到与它离开时完全相同的所有内容。

sentences.en: Or it can get garbage collected after a TTL and disappear without a trace.
sentences.zh: 或者它可以在 TTL 后被垃圾收集并消失得无影无踪。

blocks.html_en: With a SandboxWarmPool, already-started sandboxes can be assigned in milliseconds instead of waiting for a cold Pod to schedule, pull an image, and start. Cold-start latency still depends on your cluster, scheduler, image, and runtime.

sentences.en: With a SandboxWarmPool, already-started sandboxes can be assigned in milliseconds instead of waiting for a cold Pod to schedule, pull an image, and start.
sentences.zh: 使用 SandboxWarmPool，可以在几毫秒内分配已启动的沙箱，而无需等待冷 Pod 进行调度、拉取映像并启动。

sentences.en: Cold-start latency still depends on your cluster, scheduler, image, and runtime.
sentences.zh: 冷启动延迟仍然取决于您的集群、调度程序、映像和运行时。

blocks.html_en: The Architecture: CRDs All the Way Down

sentences.en: The Architecture: CRDs All the Way Down

blocks.html_en: The whole thing is built on Kubernetes custom resource definitions. There are four main ones that matter:

sentences.en: The whole thing is built on Kubernetes custom resource definitions.
sentences.zh: 整个事情都是建立在 Kubernetes 自定义资源定义之上的。

sentences.en: There are four main ones that matter:
sentences.zh: 有四个主要因素很重要：

blocks.html_en: 1. Sandbox (the core)

sentences.en: Sandbox (the core)
sentences.zh: 沙箱（核心）

blocks.html_en: This is the primitive. A single, stateful Pod with a stable hostname, optional persistent storage, and full lifecycle management. You create this, and the controller handles the rest -- Pod creation, network identity, volume provisioning, scheduled deletion, pausing, and resuming.

sentences.en: This is the primitive.
sentences.zh: 这是原始的。

sentences.en: A single, stateful Pod with a stable hostname, optional persistent storage, and full lifecycle management.
sentences.zh: 具有稳定主机名、可选持久存储和完整生命周期管理的单个有状态 Pod。

sentences.en: You create this, and the controller handles the rest -- Pod creation, network identity, volume provisioning, scheduled deletion, pausing, and resuming.
sentences.zh: 您创建它，控制器处理其余的事情——Pod 创建、网络身份、卷配置、计划删除、暂停和恢复。

blocks.html_en: It is the answer to the question: "I want a Linux box that stays alive for my agent. How do I get one?"

sentences.en: It is the answer to the question: "I want a Linux box that stays alive for my agent.
sentences.zh: 这是对以下问题的回答：“我想要一个能够为我的特工保持活力的 Linux 盒子。

sentences.en: How do I get one?"
sentences.zh: 我怎样才能得到一个？”

blocks.html_en: 2. SandboxTemplate (the blueprint)

sentences.en: SandboxTemplate (the blueprint)
sentences.zh: SandboxTemplate（蓝图）

blocks.html_en: Tired of writing the same YAML over and over? Templates let you codify runtime configuration once -- image, resource limits, runtime class (gVisor, Kata, standard), network policies, environment variables -- and reuse them everywhere. Platform teams define the templates. Developers just pick one and go.

sentences.en: Tired of writing the same YAML over and over?
sentences.zh: 厌倦了一遍又一遍地编写相同的 YAML？

sentences.en: Templates let you codify runtime configuration once -- image, resource limits, runtime class (gVisor, Kata, standard), network policies, environment variables -- and reuse them everywhere.
sentences.zh: 模板可让您编写一次运行时配置——图像​​、资源限制、运行时类（gVisor、Kata、标准）、网络策略、环境变量——并在任何地方重用它们。

sentences.en: Platform teams define the templates.
sentences.zh: 平台团队定义模板。

sentences.en: Developers just pick one and go.
sentences.zh: 开发人员只需选择一个即可。

blocks.html_en: 3. SandboxClaim (the request)

sentences.en: SandboxClaim (the request)
sentences.zh: SandboxClaim（请求）

blocks.html_en: This is the user-facing abstraction. In the current v1beta1 API, a developer or agent SDK creates a SandboxClaim that references a SandboxWarmPool. The warm pool references the SandboxTemplate. The controller adopts an available pre-warmed sandbox from that pool, or creates capacity according to the pool configuration, and hands back a ready-to-use environment.

sentences.en: This is the user-facing abstraction.
sentences.zh: 这是面向用户的抽象。

sentences.en: In the current v1beta1 API, a developer or agent SDK creates a SandboxClaim that references a SandboxWarmPool.
sentences.zh: 在当前的 v1beta1 API 中，开发人员或代理 SDK 创建引用 SandboxWarmPool 的 SandboxClaim。

sentences.en: The warm pool references the SandboxTemplate.
sentences.zh: 温池引用SandboxTemplate。

sentences.en: The controller adopts an available pre-warmed sandbox from that pool, or creates capacity according to the pool configuration, and hands back a ready-to-use environment.
sentences.zh: 控制器采用该池中可用的预热沙箱，或根据池配置创建容量，并交回现成的环境。

blocks.html_en: This is the Claim Model in action. You separate the what (I need a sandbox) from the how (here is where it runs on the cluster). And honestly? This is the pattern Kubernetes has needed for stateful workloads for a long time.

sentences.en: This is the Claim Model in action.
sentences.zh: 这是实际的索赔模型。

sentences.en: You separate the what (I need a sandbox) from the how (here is where it runs on the cluster).
sentences.zh: 您将内容（我需要一个沙箱）与方式（这里是它在集群上运行的位置）分开。

sentences.en: And honestly?
sentences.zh: 老实说？

sentences.en: This is the pattern Kubernetes has needed for stateful workloads for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这是 Kubernetes 长期以来有状态工作负载所需的模式。

blocks.html_en: 4. SandboxWarmPool (the performance hack)

sentences.en: SandboxWarmPool (the performance hack)
sentences.zh: SandboxWarmPool（性能黑客）

blocks.html_en: Here is where it gets fast. A SandboxWarmPool maintains a set of pre-warmed Pod instances in a ready state. When a claim comes in, the controller instantly assigns a Pod from the pool instead of waiting for image pulls and container startup.

sentences.en: Here is where it gets fast.
sentences.zh: 这就是它变得很快的地方。

sentences.en: A SandboxWarmPool maintains a set of pre-warmed Pod instances in a ready state.
sentences.zh: SandboxWarmPool 维护一组处于就绪状态的预热 Pod 实例。

sentences.en: When a claim comes in, the controller instantly assigns a Pod from the pool instead of waiting for image pulls and container startup.
sentences.zh: 当收到声明时，控制器会立即从池中分配一个 Pod，而不是等待镜像拉取和容器启动。

blocks.html_en: Warm pools reduce provisioning latency by keeping Sandbox instances pre-created and ready to be claimed. On GKE, Pod snapshots are a separate feature that can save and restore sandbox state for pause/resume and faster recovery; they are not required for a warm pool to work.

sentences.en: Warm pools reduce provisioning latency by keeping Sandbox instances pre-created and ready to be claimed.
sentences.zh: 温池通过保持沙盒实例预先创建并准备好声明来减少配置延迟。

sentences.en: On GKE, Pod snapshots are a separate feature that can save and restore sandbox state for pause/resume and faster recovery; they are not required for a warm pool to work.
sentences.zh: 在 GKE 上，Pod 快照是一项单独的功能，可以保存和恢复沙箱状态以进行暂停/恢复和更快的恢复；温水池的工作不需要它们。

blocks.html_en: Security: Default Deny Is the Only Way

sentences.en: Security: Default Deny Is the Only Way
sentences.zh: 安全：默认拒绝是唯一的方法

blocks.html_en: Here is something that does not get talked about enough. When you give an agent a Linux box, you are trusting it with network access. A lot of agent sandbox solutions just throw a container at you and say "good luck".

sentences.en: Here is something that does not get talked about enough.
sentences.zh: 这是一些没有被充分讨论的事情。

sentences.en: When you give an agent a Linux box, you are trusting it with network access.
sentences.zh: 当您向代理提供 Linux 机器时，您就信任它具有网络访问权限。

sentences.en: A lot of agent sandbox solutions just throw a container at you and say "good luck".
sentences.zh: 许多代理沙箱解决方案只是向您扔一个容器并说“祝您好运”。

blocks.html_en: GKE Agent Sandbox implements a Default Deny network security posture. Out of the box, code inside a sandbox cannot access your internal networks, your GKE control plane, or anything it should not. You explicitly define allowed egress and ingress rules in your SandboxTemplate.

sentences.en: GKE Agent Sandbox implements a Default Deny network security posture.
sentences.zh: GKE Agent Sandbox 实施默认拒绝网络安全态势。

sentences.en: Out of the box, code inside a sandbox cannot access your internal networks, your GKE control plane, or anything it should not.
sentences.zh: 开箱即用后，沙箱内的代码无法访问您的内部网络、GKE 控制平面或任何不应访问的内容。

sentences.en: You explicitly define allowed egress and ingress rules in your SandboxTemplate.
sentences.zh: 您可以在 SandboxTemplate 中明确定义允许的出口和入口规则。

blocks.html_en: Why does this matter? Because the most realistic threat from LLM-generated code is not "the AI becomes self-aware and takes over the world". It is "the AI wrote a Python script with a typo that accidentally hit the production database". Default deny prevents the accident. Fine-grained rules let you open specific doors when you need to (e.g., pip needs to reach PyPI, your agent needs to call an API).

sentences.en: Why does this matter?
sentences.zh: 为什么这很重要？

blocks.html_en: Agent Sandbox solves a real problem that has been getting more urgent by the month. As LLMs get better at generating code, the volume of untrusted code being executed in agent loops is going to explode. Every one of those executions is an opportunity for something to go wrong.

sentences.en: Agent Sandbox solves a real problem that has been getting more urgent by the month.
sentences.zh: Agent Sandbox 解决了一个日益紧迫的实际问题。

sentences.en: As LLMs get better at generating code, the volume of untrusted code being executed in agent loops is going to explode.
sentences.zh: 随着法学硕士在生成代码方面做得越来越好，代理循环中执行的不受信任的代码量将会呈爆炸式增长。

sentences.en: Every one of those executions is an opportunity for something to go wrong.
sentences.zh: 每一次处决都是出现问题的机会。

blocks.html_en: The old approach was: "just run it in a Docker container, it will be fine." A container can absolutely have a hostname and persistent volumes, but a one-off Docker workflow does not give you the Kubernetes-native Sandbox lifecycle, claim/warm-pool allocation model, controller-managed identity, or stronger isolation runtime by itself. Those are the abstractions Agent Sandbox is adding.

sentences.en: The old approach was: "just run it in a Docker container, it will be fine."
sentences.zh: 旧的方法是：“只要在 Docker 容器中运行它就可以了。”

sentences.en: A container can absolutely have a hostname and persistent volumes, but a one-off Docker workflow does not give you the Kubernetes-native Sandbox lifecycle, claim/warm-pool allocation model, controller-managed identity, or stronger isolation runtime by itself.
sentences.zh: 容器绝对可以拥有主机名和持久卷，但一次性 Docker 工作流程本身无法为您提供 Kubernetes 原生沙盒生命周期、声明/热池分配模型、控制器管理的身份或更强大的隔离运行时。

sentences.en: Those are the abstractions Agent Sandbox is adding.
sentences.zh: 这些是 Agent Sandbox 添加的抽象。

blocks.html_en: Agent Sandbox gives you those lifecycle and allocation primitives on top of Kubernetes, with SDKs in Python and Go. Isolation strength still depends on the runtime you configure; the managed GKE feature enforces gVisor for sandbox workloads.

sentences.en: Agent Sandbox gives you those lifecycle and allocation primitives on top of Kubernetes, with SDKs in Python and Go.
sentences.zh: Agent Sandbox 为您提供了 Kubernetes 之上的生命周期和分配原语，以及 Python 和 Go 中的 SDK。

sentences.en: Isolation strength still depends on the runtime you configure; the managed GKE feature enforces gVisor for sandbox workloads.
sentences.zh: 隔离强度仍然取决于您配置的运行时；托管 GKE 功能针对沙箱工作负载强制执行 gVisor。

blocks.html_en: The open-source project under kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox is the bedrock. Google's managed GKE add-on is the "press this button and it works" version. Both are worth knowing about.

sentences.en: The open-source project under kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox is the bedrock.
sentences.zh: kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox 下的开源项目是基础。

sentences.en: Google's managed GKE add-on is the "press this button and it works" version.
sentences.zh: Google 托管的 GKE 插件是“按下此按钮即可运行”版本。

sentences.en: Both are worth knowing about.
sentences.zh: 两者都值得了解。

sentences.en: A Reality Check (Because Nothing Is Perfect)
sentences.zh: 现实检验（因为没有什么是完美的）

blocks.html_en: Latency is low but not zero. Even with warm pools and Pod snapshots, you are looking at hundreds of milliseconds to a second for sandbox assignment. For most agent use cases that is fine. For real-time loops that need sub-100ms responses, you will feel it.

sentences.en: Latency is low but not zero.
sentences.zh: 延迟很低，但不是零。

sentences.en: Even with warm pools and Pod snapshots, you are looking at hundreds of milliseconds to a second for sandbox assignment.
sentences.zh: 即使使用热池和 Pod 快照，沙箱分配也需要数百毫秒到一秒的时间。

sentences.en: For most agent use cases that is fine.
sentences.zh: 对于大多数代理用例来说这很好。

sentences.en: For real-time loops that need sub-100ms responses, you will feel it.
sentences.zh: 对于需要 100 毫秒以下响应的实时循环，您会感觉到的。

blocks.html_en: State management is your problem. A sandbox is stateful by design. But what happens when an agent session crashes mid-execution? Do you keep the sandbox around? For how long? The TTL feature helps, but designing your garbage collection strategy is on you.

sentences.en: State management is your problem.
sentences.zh: 状态管理是你的问题。

sentences.en: A sandbox is stateful by design.
sentences.zh: 沙箱在设计上是有状态的。

sentences.en: But what happens when an agent session crashes mid-execution?
sentences.zh: 但是，当代理会话在执行过程中崩溃时会发生什么？

sentences.en: Do you keep the sandbox around?
sentences.zh: 你保留沙箱吗？

sentences.en: For how long?
sentences.zh: 多长时间？

sentences.en: The TTL feature helps, but designing your garbage collection strategy is on you.
sentences.zh: TTL 功能会有所帮助，但设计垃圾收集策略则取决于您。

blocks.html_en: Network policy complexity is real. Default deny is great for security. But the first time your agent cannot pip install because egress to PyPI is blocked, you will spend time debugging. And the first time a client's script needs to reach an internal API, you will be writing policy rules. It is manageable. But it is not zero-effort.

sentences.en: Network policy complexity is real.
sentences.zh: 网络策略的复杂性是真实存在的。

sentences.en: Default deny is great for security.
sentences.zh: 默认拒绝对于安全性非常有用。

sentences.en: But the first time your agent cannot pip install because egress to PyPI is blocked, you will spend time debugging.
sentences.zh: 但是，第一次您的代理无法 pip install 因为 PyPI 的出口被阻止，您将花费时间进行调试。

sentences.en: And the first time a client's script needs to reach an internal API, you will be writing policy rules.
sentences.zh: 当客户端的脚本第一次需要访问内部 API 时，您将编写策略规则。

sentences.en: It is manageable.
sentences.zh: 这是可以管理的。

sentences.en: But it is not zero-effort.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是零努力。

blocks.html_en: Costs add up in warm pools. Each pre-warmed Pod is a running container burning CPU and memory while it waits. If you keep a pool of 20 sandboxes hot, you are paying for 20 idle containers. The pause/resume via Pod snapshots helps offset this, but it is something to budget for.

sentences.en: Costs add up in warm pools.
sentences.zh: 温水池的成本会增加。

sentences.en: Each pre-warmed Pod is a running container burning CPU and memory while it waits.
sentences.zh: 每个预热的 Pod 都是一个正在运行的容器，在等待时会消耗 CPU 和内存。

sentences.en: If you keep a pool of 20 sandboxes hot, you are paying for 20 idle containers.
sentences.zh: 如果您保持 20 个沙盒池的热状态，那么您就要为 20 个闲置容器付费。

sentences.en: The pause/resume via Pod snapshots helps offset this, but it is something to budget for.
sentences.zh: 通过 Pod 快照进行的暂停/恢复有助于抵消这一点，但这是需要预算的。

blocks.html_en: Monitoring is a blank canvas. Your existing Kubernetes monitoring? Probably set up for Deployments and StatefulSets. Ephemeral sandboxes that live for seconds to minutes are a different monitoring challenge. Log aggregation, metrics collection, cost attribution -- you are building some of this yourself.

sentences.zh: 监控是一张空白画布。

sentences.en: Your existing Kubernetes monitoring?
sentences.zh: 您现有的 Kubernetes 监控？

sentences.en: Probably set up for Deployments and StatefulSets.
sentences.zh: 可能是为 Deployments 和 StatefulSets 设置的。

sentences.en: Ephemeral sandboxes that live for seconds to minutes are a different monitoring challenge.
sentences.zh: 存在数秒到几分钟的短暂沙箱是一个不同的监控挑战。

sentences.en: Log aggregation, metrics collection, cost attribution -- you are building some of this yourself.
sentences.zh: 日志聚合、指标收集、成本归因——您正在自己构建其中的一些内容。

content_html_zh:
来源：GKE Agent Sandbox 文档、kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox

所以事情就是这样。 我们要求人工智能代理做越来越疯狂的事情。 写代码。 浏览网页。 运行外壳命令。 启动浏览器。 单击周围。 部署网站。 像人一样使用计算机。 大多数情况下，他们正在这样做。

但有一个潜在的问题让平台工程师夜不能寐。

这段代码到底运行在哪里？

当您要求代理“运行此脚本”或“安装此软件包”或“检查该端点是否响应”时，您实际上是将一把上膛的枪交给了一位非常热情的实习生，他读过所有编程书籍，但生存本能绝对为零。 该代码可能是恶意的。 或者越野车。 或者它可能会在您的主机系统上进行核处理，因为代理决定 rm -rf / 认为它正在清理临时文件。

这就是代理沙盒的用武之地。

将它们视为为每个代理提供了自己密封的一次性 Linux 容器。 一个小小的虚拟机婴儿床。 带有橡胶墙的婴儿围栏，它们可以在其中跑来跑去并破坏东西，而无需接触您真正的基础设施。

更重要的是：这不是某种汽件未来概念。 Google Cloud 将 Agent Sandbox 作为托管 GKE 功能提供，并且 Kubernetes API 背后的开源项目位于 kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox 下。 您可以在自己的 Kubernetes 集群上运行开源控制器或使用托管 GKE 集成。

GKE Agent 沙盒到底是什么

让我直接引用文档，这样我们就可以达成共识：

“GKE Agent Sandbox 可帮助您管理 GKE 上的隔离、有状态和单副本工作负载。 它针对 AI 代理运行时等用例进行了优化，其中不受信任的 LLM 生成的代码必须在安全且高性能的环境中执行。”

用简单的英语来说，这意味着：

您可以通过 Kubernetes 原生方式来启动单个有状态容器，其行为类似于轻量级虚拟机。 它具有稳定的主机名、可在重新启动后继续存在的持久存储、内核级隔离以及默认为“拒绝所有”的网络策略。 您的代理可以连接到它，执行其操作，断开连接，稍后再回来，并找到与它离开时完全相同的所有内容。 或者它可以在 TTL 后被垃圾收集并消失得无影无踪。

使用 SandboxWarmPool，可以在几毫秒内分配已启动的沙箱，而无需等待冷 Pod 进行调度、拉取映像并启动。 冷启动延迟仍然取决于您的集群、调度程序、映像和运行时。

架构：CRD 一直向下

整个事情都是建立在 Kubernetes 自定义资源定义之上的。 有四个主要因素很重要：

1. 沙箱（核心）

这是原始的。 具有稳定主机名、可选持久存储和完整生命周期管理的单个有状态 Pod。 您创建它，控制器处理其余的事情——Pod 创建、网络身份、卷配置、计划删除、暂停和恢复。

这是对以下问题的回答：“我想要一个能够为我的特工保持活力的 Linux 盒子。 我怎样才能得到一个？”

2. SandboxTemplate（蓝图）

厌倦了一遍又一遍地编写相同的 YAML？ 模板可让您编写一次运行时配置——图像​​、资源限制、运行时类（gVisor、Kata、标准）、网络策略、环境变量——并在任何地方重用它们。 平台团队定义模板。 开发人员只需选择一个即可。

3. SandboxClaim（请求）

这是面向用户的抽象。 在当前的 v1beta1 API 中，开发人员或代理 SDK 创建引用 SandboxWarmPool 的 SandboxClaim。 温池引用SandboxTemplate。 控制器采用该池中可用的预热沙箱，或根据池配置创建容量，并交回现成的环境。

这是实际的索赔模型。 您将内容（我需要一个沙箱）与方式（这里是它在集群上运行的位置）分开。 老实说？ 这是 Kubernetes 长期以来有状态工作负载所需的模式。

4. SandboxWarmPool（性能黑客）

这就是它变得很快的地方。 SandboxWarmPool 维护一组处于就绪状态的预热 Pod 实例。 当收到声明时，控制器会立即从池中分配一个 Pod，而不是等待镜像拉取和容器启动。

温池通过保持沙盒实例预先创建并准备好声明来减少配置延迟。 在 GKE 上，Pod 快照是一项单独的功能，可以保存和恢复沙箱状态以进行暂停/恢复和更快的恢复；温水池的工作不需要它们。

安全：默认拒绝是唯一的方法

这是一些没有被充分讨论的事情。 当您向代理提供 Linux 机器时，您就信任它具有网络访问权限。 许多代理沙箱解决方案只是向您扔一个容器并说“祝您好运”。

GKE Agent Sandbox 实施默认拒绝网络安全态势。 开箱即用后，沙箱内的代码无法访问您的内部网络、GKE 控制平面或任何不应访问的内容。 您可以在 SandboxTemplate 中明确定义允许的出口和入口规则。

为什么这很重要？ 因为LLM生成的代码最现实的威胁不是“人工智能变得有自我意识并接管世界”。 这是“AI 编写了一个带有拼写错误的 Python 脚本，不小心击中了生产数据库”。 默认拒绝可以防止事故发生。 细粒度的规则可让您在需要时打开特定的门（例如，pip 需要到达 PyPI，您的代理需要调用 API）。

隔离运行时：选择你的毒药

沙箱 CRD 与运行时无关。 您可以将其与：

  • 标准容器——快速、熟悉，但工作负载之间的隔离程度最低
  • gVisor——Google 的用户空间内核。 在容器和主机内核之间提供第二个安全边界。 这是不可信代码执行的建议默认值。
  • Kata Containers——硬件级虚拟机隔离。 每个沙箱都有自己的轻量级虚拟机和自己的内核。 最重的隔离，但也是最强的。

API 的美妙之处在于，在这些 API 之间进行切换是 SandboxTemplate 中的字段更改。 您无需重新设计您的架构。 您只需更改runtimeClassName。

编程访问 SDK

您无需编写 Kubernetes YAML 即可使用它。 有一流的客户端库：

  • Python SDK——LangChain、Vertex AI Agentic SDK 或任何 Python 代理框架的高级客户端。 通过代理代码创建、查询、管理和销毁沙箱。
  • Go SDK——供平台工程师在 Agent Sandbox 之上构建控制器和服务。

这两个 SDK 都抽象了索赔生命周期。 使用当前的Python SDK，您的代理使用client.create_sandbox（warmpool =“python-sandbox-pool”，namespace =“default”）创建沙箱。 在幕后，SDK 创建一个 SandboxClaim，控制器从热池中分配一个 Sandbox，客户端返回一个用于命令执行和文件操作的句柄。

实用要点

Agent Sandbox 解决了一个日益紧迫的实际问题。 随着法学硕士在生成代码方面做得越来越好，代理循环中执行的不受信任的代码量将会呈爆炸式增长。 每一次处决都是出现问题的机会。

旧的方法是：“只要在 Docker 容器中运行它就可以了。” 容器绝对可以拥有主机名和持久卷，但一次性 Docker 工作流程本身无法为您提供 Kubernetes 原生沙盒生命周期、声明/热池分配模型、控制器管理的身份或更强大的隔离运行时。 这些是 Agent Sandbox 添加的抽象。

Agent Sandbox 为您提供了 Kubernetes 之上的生命周期和分配原语，以及 Python 和 Go 中的 SDK。 隔离强度仍然取决于您配置的运行时；托管 GKE 功能针对沙箱工作负载强制执行 gVisor。

kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox 下的开源项目是基础。 Google 托管的 GKE 插件是“按下此按钮即可运行”版本。 两者都值得了解。

现实检验（因为没有什么是完美的）

延迟很低，但不是零。 即使使用热池和 Pod 快照，沙箱分配也需要数百毫秒到一秒的时间。 对于大多数代理用例来说这很好。 对于需要 100 毫秒以下响应的实时循环，您会感觉到的。

状态管理是你的问题。 沙箱在设计上是有状态的。 但是，当代理会话在执行过程中崩溃时会发生什么？ 你保留沙箱吗？ 多长时间？ TTL 功能会有所帮助，但设计垃圾收集策略则取决于您。

网络策略的复杂性是真实存在的。 默认拒绝对于安全性非常有用。 但是，第一次您的代理无法 pip install 因为 PyPI 的出口被阻止，您将花费时间进行调试。 当客户端的脚本第一次需要访问内部 API 时，您将编写策略规则。 这是可以管理的。 但这并不是零努力。

温水池的成本会增加。 每个预热的 Pod 都是一个正在运行的容器，在等待时会消耗 CPU 和内存。 如果您保持 20 个沙盒池的热状态，那么您就要为 20 个闲置容器付费。 通过 Pod 快照进行的暂停/恢复有助于抵消这一点，但这是需要预算的。

监控是一张空白画布。 您现有的 Kubernetes 监控？ 可能是为 Deployments 和 StatefulSets 设置的。 存在数秒到几分钟的短暂沙箱是一个不同的监控挑战。 日志聚合、指标收集、成本归因——您正在自己构建其中的一些内容。

入门

如果您想在新的 Kubernetes 集群上重现开源设置，请完成以下顺序：安装控制器和扩展，创建可执行的 Python 运行时模板，创建热池，为集群内客户端提供所需的 RBAC，并从普通的 Python Pod 运行 SDK。

下面的命令有意使用 kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'，因此您不需要在本地编写 YAML 文件。

1. 使用扩展 CRDs 安装 Agent Sandbox

截至撰写本文时，当前的上游版本是 v0.5.3。 固定版本使示例可重现，而不是在新版本发布时默默地更改。

export VERSION="v0.5.3"

kubectl apply -f \
  https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox/releases/download/${VERSION}/sandbox-with-extensions.yaml

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

等待控制器组件出现：

kubectl get pods -n agent-sandbox-system

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

验证是否已安装核心 API 和扩展 API：

kubectl api-resources | grep -i sandbox

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

您应该看到包括沙箱、沙箱声明、沙箱模板和沙箱热池在内的资源。

2. 创建Python运行时模板和暖池

具有 sleep 无限的普通 python:3.12-slim 容器对于 sandbox.commands.run() 来说是不够的。 SDK 将 HTTP 请求发送到端口 8888 上的运行时的 /execute 端点，因此沙箱映像必须实现该 API。

上游 Python 运行时映像正是这样做的：

kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: SandboxTemplate
metadata:
  name: python-sandbox-template
  namespace: default
spec:
  podTemplate:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: python-sandbox
        image: registry.k8s.io/agent-sandbox/python-runtime-sandbox:v0.1.0
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8888
---
apiVersion: extensions.agents.x-k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: SandboxWarmPool
metadata:
  name: python-sandbox-pool
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  sandboxTemplateRef:
    name: python-sandbox-template
EOF

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

验证模板、池、Sandbox 和 Pod 是否存在：

kubectl get sandboxtemplates,sandboxwarmpools,sandboxes,pods -n default

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

等待温池沙箱 Pod 运行。

3. 为SDK客户端创建专用的ServiceAccount和RBAC

不要在实际部署中使用命名空间的默认 ServiceAccount 运行 SDK。 为客户端提供自己的 ServiceAccount 以及创建/删除声明和解析底层沙箱所需的权限。

kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: sandbox-client
  namespace: default
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: sandbox-client
  namespace: default
rules:
- apiGroups:
  - agents.x-k8s.io
  resources:
  - sandboxes
  verbs:
  - get
  - list
  - watch
- apiGroups:
  - extensions.agents.x-k8s.io
  resources:
  - sandboxclaims
  verbs:
  - get
  - list
  - watch
  - create
  - delete
- apiGroups:
  - extensions.agents.x-k8s.io
  resources:
  - sandboxwarmpools
  - sandboxtemplates
  verbs:
  - get
  - list
  - watch
- apiGroups:
  - ""
  resources:
  - pods
  - services
  verbs:
  - get
  - list
  - watch
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: sandbox-client
  namespace: default
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: sandbox-client
  namespace: default
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: sandbox-client
EOF

kubectl auth can-i get sandboxes.agents.x-k8s.io \

  --as=system:serviceaccount:default:sandbox-client \

4. 启动 Python 客户端 Pod

SDK 可以使用 kubectl port-forward 在本地运行，但该模式需要在运行 Python 进程的环境中使用 kubectl。 对于这个可重现的示例，在集群内运行客户端并使用 SandboxInClusterConnectionConfig，它直接连接到沙箱运行时并且不会生成 kubectl。

kubectl run python-pod \
  --image=python:3.12-slim \
  --restart=Never \
  --overrides='{"spec":{"serviceAccountName":"sandbox-client"}}' \
  --command -- sleep infinity

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

等等吧：

kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/python-pod -n default --timeout=120s

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

在该 Pod 中安装 Python SDK，固定到上面使用的控制器版本：

kubectl exec -n default python-pod -- \
  pip install k8s-agent-sandbox==0.5.3

5. 创建一个沙箱并在其中执行Python

直接通过stdin运行客户端；不需要 Python 文件：

kubectl exec -i -n default python-pod -- python - <<'PY'
from k8s_agent_sandbox import SandboxClient
from k8s_agent_sandbox.models import SandboxInClusterConnectionConfig

client = SandboxClient(
    connection_config=SandboxInClusterConnectionConfig()
)

sandbox = client.create_sandbox(
    warmpool="python-sandbox-pool",
    namespace="default",
)

try:
    result = sandbox.commands.run(
        'python3 -c \'print("hello from my sandbox")\''
    )
    print(result.stdout)
finally:
    sandbox.terminate()
PY

在 GKE 上

对于托管 GKE 功能，Agent Sandbox 需要 GKE 1.35.2-gke.1269000 或更高版本。 在现有的标准集群上，Google 在启用 Agent Sandbox 之前还需要启用 gVisor 的节点池。 当前命令使用 beta 集群表面并包括集群位置：

gcloud beta container clusters update "${CLUSTER_NAME}" \
  --location="${LOCATION}" \
  --enable-agent-sandbox

进入全屏模式 退出全屏模式

GKE 还强制执行沙箱工作负载要求，例如 runtimeClassName: gvisor、禁用自动 ServiceAccount 令牌挂载、以非 root 身份运行、删除 Linux 功能、设置 CPU/内存限制以及调度到 gVisor 沙箱节点池。 使用官方 GKE 指南中的托管 GKE 部署清单，而不是上面的最小自我管理模板。

底线

当有人最终为代理运行时构建正确的抽象时，就会发生 GKE Agent Sandbox 以及它所基于的开源 kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox 项目。 它是 Kubernetes 原生的，这意味着它可以融入现有的基础设施，而无需与之对抗。 它的速度足够快，适合交互式使用。 默认情况下它是安全的。 它的 SDK 可以让代理以编程方式管理自己的环境。

“只需在 Docker 中运行并祈祷”的时代即将结束。 “给代理一个自己的Linux盒子，适当隔离，适当管理，适当快速”的时代已经到来。

老实说？ 该死的时间到了。
